packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-20 - unverified image reading (first reader)

No identification of the work or author was revealed in my context. Blind reading.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview, face 1)
- Four small separate parchment scraps laid in a row on black background, colour chart lower left, cm scale at right edge. Each scrap roughly 3.5-4.5 cm wide.
- Modern pencil labels on the scraps: "Frg. 246-4r" (leftmost), "Stams, StA, Frg. 246-3r" (second), "Frg. 246-2r" (third), "Frg. 246-1r" (rightmost; upper part of this scrap is covered by a grey rectangle in the overview).
- Text survives only along the top edge of each scrap: about 3-4 lines of a small gothic textura/semi-textura in brown-black ink. Below that the scraps are blank (lower margin, apparently). Several scraps carry a red numeral in the line (e.g. ".109." and ".99.") - look like red-ink numbers set within/at end of text lines (tentative: rubricated numbering or line-fillers; observation only).
- Leftmost scrap (246-4r) also shows, to the right of a narrow gap, line-ends of a second column/text block ("5", "so", "fe..." visible at right edge) - so two columns or text + marginal entries may be present (tentative).
- These are clearly cut-down strips; only the bottom lines of a text block survive on each.

TILE image-002.jpg (native tile; left = scrap "Frg. 246-4r", right = scrap "Frg. 246-3r", face 1 / recto side per labels)
Read via crop-01.jpg (246-4r text strip, upscaled) and crop-02.jpg (246-3r text strip, upscaled). Line numbers counted from top of image-002.

Scrap 246-4r, main text block (left part; left edge cut, so line-starts lost):
image-002 l.1: ..tisfac(ti)o? ei [illegible 1-2 words, abraded] de iou? / lou?
image-002 l.2: ..h(?) de s(?)la(?) [illegible] tacie mu-   (or "..? de sla[..]tacie nu-"; hyphen-like stroke at end)
image-002 l.3: dicat(ur)? (pro)p(ter)? [blank space]  red numeral ".109." (in the line, after text)
image-002 l.4: satisfacie(n)d(um)? [abraded ?e] diuice? / dimitte?   (last word very uncertain: "duice"/"dinice")
Scrap 246-4r, separate text at right edge past a gap (second column or adjacent text, only 1-3 letters each):
image-002 l.1: q / g (single letter, possibly "q" with stroke)
image-002 l.2: f.. (?)
image-002 l.3: fer / scr? 
image-002 l.4: so sor.. / so sou..
Observation: the red ".109." stands in a space within the line, roughly mid-column, followed by blank to the column edge - looks like a numbered paragraph/section end marker or a cross-reference number (interpretation tentative).

Scrap 246-3r (text only in the upper right of the scrap; left part of strip blank, so this is likely right-hand portion of a line block with left margin? - actually text starts about mid-scrap, so left area is blank margin or the lines were indented; uncertain):
image-002 l.0 (cut top line, only descender/lower halves): [..]tis? go no [..]  - [illegible]
image-002 l.1: xp(ist)i? / ipm? et s(ecundu)m? loz? / lo(rum)? di[..]? qui e(t)ia(m) tu-
image-002 l.2: posset s(?)[..] mouere? / [..]ouere ex?   [blank]  red numeral ".99."
image-002 l.3: uali? / nali? debet? / debeat? [abraded] [..]bil.. / abil..   (end abraded at tear)
Notes: "qui e(t)ia(m)" fairly clear; "posset" fairly clear; the red ".99." is placed at line-end after a gap as on 246-4r.

TILE image-003.jpg (native tile; left = right part of 246-3r again (overlap with image-002, not new text), centre = scrap "Frg. 246-2r", right = scrap "Frg. 246-1r" whose text area is covered by a grey rectangle)
Overlap: the left edge shows 246-3r lines "..oz di[..] qui e(t)ia(m) tu-" / "..[m]ouere ex .99." / "..debet.. ..bil.." - same lines as image-002, not counted again.
Scrap 246-1r: everything above the pencil label is hidden by a grey rectangle in this tile (and in the overview). No text visible to me; nothing read.
Scrap 246-2r read via crop-03.jpg (upscaled). Text sits at the left edge of the scrap (left edge cut, so line-starts are lost); right of the text is blank parchment, so these appear to be line-ends of a column followed by margin (tentative). Line numbers from top of image-003:
image-003 l.1: ..a (con)clusi(on)e? / (con)cl(us)io(n)e?   (ꝯ-sign before "cl"; long tail stroke over the end)
image-003 l.2: ..u · (cir)cu(m)? / [r]cũ? oli̅ / o(mn)i?   ("cu" with macron below/above; "oli" with a flourished stroke above; expansion uncertain)
image-003 l.3: ..ro: (er)g(o)? / q(uo)? un-a / uu-a?   (letter with superscript o; hyphen-like stroke between "un" and "a")
image-003 l.4: ..lustru(m)? / lustriu(m)?  followed by a point "." and blank - line ends here.
No rubrics or red numerals visible on 246-2r.

LAYOUT SURVEY, face 2 (image-004.jpg, overview): same four scraps turned over, pencil labels "Frg. 246-4v", "Stams, StA, Frg. 246-3v", "Frg. 246-2v", "Frg. 246-1v". No grey mask on this face.
- 246-4v: text traces along the right edge (vertical strip of line-ends/starts), faint; possibly some red at upper left edge.
- 246-3v: 3-4 lines along the top edge, with a red mark (numeral?) under the text.
- 246-2v: a few short lines at upper right.
- 246-1v: heavily stained/orange, damaged; no clear text in the overview (perhaps faint traces).

TILE image-005.jpg (native tile; left = "Frg. 246-4v", right = "Stams, StA, Frg. 246-3v")
Line numbers from top of image-005. Read via crop-04.jpg (246-3v strip) and crop-05.jpg (246-4v strip), both upscaled.

Scrap 246-3v (text across the top of the scrap, left side; line-starts at left edge partly lost to a tear at upper left; top line cut by the edge):
image-005 l.1 (upper halves partly cut): ..icit? / ..cit? q(uod)? fact(um)? / facto̅? [..] nu̅? hoc fuerit? / fec[..]   ("hoc" clear; rest uncertain)
image-005 l.2: [..] [illegible, abraded] .. [..]tis? / ..d̅ce? [illegible] Paul(us)? / man(us)?   (last word: P/m + "aul"/"anu" + s with flourish)
image-005 l.3: s(ed)? / f(ac)ta? fu(n)da(ta)? / fra[..] et s(ed)? / ?[..]a̅ [illegible] [..]a̅ / ua̅
image-005 l.4: [..]one? / ?o(n)e? [faint red trace] P(ri)ncip(ium)? / p(ro)p(ri)is? / ppm(us)?  [rest abraded]   (word after the faint red trace: P/p + p + m/in + i + ss/ff with superscript; very uncertain)
image-005 l.5: Aliud? / Alijs? / al(io)s? · x?  [blank / abraded]  red numeral ".111." (in the line, after a gap, as on 246-3r / 246-4r)
Note: in l.3-l.5 there is a narrow vertical sequence of letters ("d"/"q"-like at l.3-4, "x" at l.5) directly under the l.1 word "facto̅/factu(m)"; it may belong to the text or be a separate narrow entry; I could not settle this.
Note: two faint pinkish discs on l.3-l.4 near the left edge look like faded red (rubric touch or offset), not legible.

Scrap 246-4v (surface heavily abraded and stained; ink traces only):
image-005 l.1: [illegible traces] .. d? (con)?/a? [..]g? .. g? [illegible]
image-005 l.2: [illegible traces] .. ?go? .. g? [illegible]
image-005 l.3: [illegible]  faint red numeral, perhaps ".1[..]." / ".10?." - not legible
image-005 l.4: ..re? / ..te? q? (at left edge)  [illegible traces further right]
At far right edge (separate strip past a crease) traces of single letters on each line (g?, l?, s?), unreadable.
Assessment: 246-4v has no readable continuous words; I did not force readings.

TILE image-006.jpg (native tile; left edge = sliver of 246-3v (overlap, blank part), centre = "Frg. 246-2v", right = "Frg. 246-1v")
Line numbers from top of image-006.

Scrap 246-2v, read via crop-06.jpg (upscaled). Text sits at the upper right of the scrap, right edge cut; blank parchment to the left, so these look like line-starts after a left margin (tentative). Physically this is the same edge that carries the line-ends on 246-2r (consistent with recto/verso of one strip).
image-006 l.0 (cut top line): [illegible, lower parts of letters only]
image-006 l.1: ..ly? / ..u[..] detur. s(ed)? / A?   (".. detur" clear, followed by a point; then a tall letter at the cut edge)
image-006 l.2: (et)? / ꝛ ab(s)olucio(n)[em]? / absolucio̅ / abl(u)cio(n)   (reading "ꝛ" + "ab" + superscript-like stroke + "lucio" + "n" with macron; "absolucion.." is my best reading but the s is not clearly there)
image-006 l.3: [..]? q(ui)? / q(uod)? si (con)[..] / s(ecundu)m? [cut]
image-006 l.4: [abraded] .. ad
No red visible on 246-2v.

Scrap 246-1v: surface badly stained (orange/brown) and flaking, with a hole; I see no ink letters I can read. Possible faint traces at the upper left only. Nothing transcribed.

LIMITATIONS AND SUMMARY
- Four tiny cut strips; each preserves only 3-5 lines at one edge. Face 1 (r) and face 2 (v) of 246-1 to 246-4 viewed. 246-1r text was masked by a grey rectangle in every image supplied; 246-1v and 246-4v have no legible text.
- Best-secured words: "qui e(t)ia(m)", "posset" (246-3r); "..detur." , "absolucio(n)?" (246-2v); "..lustru(m)." , "(con)clusi(on)e?" (246-2r); "satisfac-" words (246-4r); "hoc" (246-3v).
- Red numerals .109. (246-4r), .99. (246-3r), .111. (246-3v) appear in-line after a gap; observation only. Whether these are chapter/section numbers or cross-references I cannot say from the images.
- Hand: small gothic book hand (textura-like), brown-black ink, heavy abbreviation (ꝯ, superscript o, macrons, q-abbreviations).
- Suggest higher-resolution or raking-light images of 246-4v, 246-3v left side and 246-1v, and an unmasked image of 246-1r.
- Crops made: crop-01.jpg, crop-02.jpg, crop-03.jpg, crop-04.jpg, crop-05.jpg, crop-06.jpg (simple crops + upscale only). Nothing done beyond the brief's rules. I did not hit the image limit.
